question: Do the committed sharp-direction and declared-Gamma_1 certificates contain the normalization-fixed nonzero-lambda sensitivity initial datum and panel tubes required to start a rigorous panelwise Picard/affine enclosure and make a sign-separation decision?

upstream_results.role: pins the six zero-containing scale-free endpoint intervals and records that the prior nonlinear term used only 0<=J_(rho^2)<=J_0
pins the lambda-zero declared-boundary derivative while explicitly excluding an actual finite nonzero-lambda family
pins the real plus-tail direction error, whose scope excludes a lambda derivative

declared_conventions.sensitivity_equation: s_x=(2+(1+2*rho)/x)*s-sqrt(x/C), where s=partial_lambda rho under one fixed plus-end normalization
declared_conventions.affine_panel_requirement: Each x panel must carry an outward rho tube, a normalization-fixed s interval at its entering boundary, and a proved Picard remainder; endpoint sign is decided only from an actual declared Gamma_1 enclosure after the complete left-tail remainder.
declared_conventions.execution: exact SymPy identity audit and committed-result schema/payload checks only; no ODE solve, quadrature, root solve, finite difference, sampling or inferred sensitivity bound

required_prerequisites.description: Outward partial_lambda rho(Q_plus) for the actual plus-recessive family under the panel normalization; checked at the pinned authoritative schema path.
Finite panel partition plus outward actual-rho tube on every panel, not merely global 0<=rho^2<=1; checked at the pinned authoritative schema path.
Sharp actual declared Gamma_1 endpoint functional with complete minus-tail remainder; requires both explicit nonnull boundary-value and minus-tail fields in the pinned boundary-variation schema.

decision_table.programme_impact: A separately specified bounded panelwise calculation may be formulated; this audit itself does not perform it.

decision_table.programme_impact: Fail closed: retain the sharp direction result, emit no sensitivity, endpoint sign, continuation or spectral inference.
